# R304 — replica lifecycle and HTTP contract for the SYCL server

## Scope and result

Read-only source audit: official pristine v0.1.43 `serve/replicas.py` and `serve/test_replicas.py` against the immutable curated baseline `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/perf-native-copy-cohorts-qualified-20261012` supplied at HEAD `840db05`. I did not read the replica implementation in progress. Registry v172 and R300/R302 were read for scope; the R302 gap inventory is not repeated here. No test, import, build, GPU, service, Git operation, cleanup, or source change was made. The only new file is this report.

The upstream adapter is a per-request engine facade, not just a router. For SYCL, carry forward the observable semantics, but rework config-to-device mapping, ownership of request-local properties, and unsupported global APIs. In particular: use stable PCI IDs for per-replica device groups; do not route SAVE/RESTORE to an arbitrary replica; use minimum live context and explicit per-replica metrics; guarantee cancellation always returns counters/locks; clear route-cache knowledge only for the engine whose cache was lost. Run all required fixtures with fake engines/processes and the real Python `Service`/HTTP server; real multi-GPU behavior remains unverified because this host has one GPU.

## Source contracts that drive the adaptation

- **Routing is a cache-cost heuristic, not a session-ID map.** `Router` (`serve/replicas.py:122–170`) chains input-token hashes in fixed 64-token blocks, keeps a replica bitmask per prefix, and bounds the index (`INDEX_MAX`). `route` compares `prompt_tokens - matched_prefix + LOAD_TOKENS * inflight` among alive replicas and breaks ties using `inflight` then `routed` (`:344–358`). Thus repeated full conversation prompts usually return to the replica with the longest verified-in-engine prefix; under load they may move elsewhere and simply reread more. The engine remains the correctness authority for its actual prefix (`:18–19`). Do not present this as sticky identity or exact cache state.
- **Route-cache ownership follows engine lifecycle.** Successful generation notes `ids + produced`; restart/unload forgets that replica (`:307–332,383–421`); nonfinite clears that replica's whole cached-prefix bit (`:410–420`). A restart of one process must not erase other replicas' prefix entries. The source also calls `router.note(k, ids)` before its serial run-lock wait (`:394–401`); cancellation while waiting can leave a prompt recorded although it never entered the engine. Treat this as a stale-cache hint risk to fix or make conservative in the adapter, and test the cancelled-before-admission case. Stale hints should affect only placement/performance, never bypass full engine validation.
- **Service concurrency and facade shape are observable.** `ReplicaEngine.batch` is the sum of each child slot count, treating a non-batched child as one slot (`:220–224`); `waiting` sums child waits (`:226–228`). The facade uses `threading.local()` to point `last`, progress and delegated properties at the child selected by `generate` (`:195–218,267–279,383–390`); outside that request thread, the fallback is child zero (`:197–203`). A selected child must not leak into unrelated server/connection threads, and a background metrics request must not silently report child zero as the whole system. Shared API settings are Service-level state (`server.py:2658–2662`) and sampling is passed into the chosen child's `generate`; it is not a per-child mutable setting.
- **The facade deliberately declines APIs that have no single owner.** Upstream `NOT_HERE` excludes `session_file`, `vram`, `ctl`, and `slot_cv` (`replicas.py:173–177,200–203`). The curated `Service.slot_action` is a single slot-zero file operation guarded by FIFO and explicit batch exclusion (`server.py:2725–2770`); `POST /v1/vram` is an engine-global resize guarded by the control/FIFO contract (`:2900–2920`). A request has no stable replica field, and the router may select a different process later. Keep slot save/restore disabled with an explicit 501 while replicas are active unless a new versioned API defines replica identity and file ownership. Never let facade fallback silently save or resize replica 0.
- **Health/context/status must be fleet-aware.** The wrapper reports alive if any child is alive, minimum context among live children, aggregate slot capacity, a replica-specific slot view with a global slot offset and owner tag, plus `replicas`/`replicas_alive` and running/routed counts (`replicas.py:221–253,281–304`). The current `Service` exposes shared state through `/health`, `/v1/status`, `/metrics`, `/metrics/prometheus`, `/slots`, `/props`, `/v1/models`, `/v1/load`, and `/v1/unload` (`server.py:3108–3185,4700+,4767+,4829+,4863+`). Preserve current response fields while adding replica detail. In upstream, `/metrics` keeps each slot's `replica` field, but the `/slots` handler rebuilds each row from only `id`, `n_ctx`, `is_processing`, and `n_prompt_tokens` (`server.py:4767–4780`); an adapted API should either add the replica owner there or explicitly define global slot IDs so an operator can map a slot to its process.
- **Diagnostics have per-process ownership.** `replica_cfg` copies config, selects child GPUs, removes the replica directive, suffixes log and expert-profile-save paths, and merges only that group's optional `env`/`args` (`replicas.py:84–106`). `ReplicaEngine.log_path`, `spawn`, and most fallback diagnostics use child zero (`:259–266,284–288`); `Service.metrics` polls one `log_cursor`/`ConvCacheLog` and constructs engine metadata from `info` (`server.py:3149–3157`). An adapter must surface selected `replica_id` with `EngineDied`/READY errors, retain a separate log cursor for each child, and not imply child-zero logs/profile/INFO describe all devices. Model/tokenizer/template and context semantics must agree across replicas; allow per-group args/env only for intended device-local differences or reject incompatible configs.

## SYCL/PCI adaptation constraints

The curated server represents the selected Intel devices by PCI address: setup writes `gpu_pci` and optional `split_pci` (`setup.py:3613–3623`); `engine_args` adds `--layer-split`/`--split-device` from the PCI list (`serve/server.py:2327–2336`); `child_env` applies config env then uses `setdefault("STRATA_GPU_PCI", gpu_pci)` (`:2443–2453`). Do not transplant `replica_cfg`'s upstream ordinal-only `c["gpu"] = gpus` logic as the device authority. Resolve numeric setup choices to PCI once, then construct each child with `gpu_pci = group[0]`, `split_pci = group[1:]`, and no inherited stale parent `STRATA_GPU_PCI` / `split_pci`. Keep child overrides from pointing back into another group's PCI set. Validate distinct PCI ownership across groups and preserve the current one-process layer-split mode as a separate configuration.

The global `Service` reads `gpu_pci` for VRAM checks and the Monitor (`server.py:2839–2868,6041`), while setup's current group is one base PCI plus `split_pci`. Replica admission/restart therefore cannot rely on the existing first-GPU-only free-VRAM result. Either preflight every PCI in each group and treat a failed group's READY as unavailable, or make the min-free policy explicitly per-group. Metrics should expose the PCI(s) per replica and distinguish per-device readings from fleet totals. Do not use CUDA-visible ordinals as a substitute for `STRATA_GPU_PCI` on SYCL.

## Required fake-engine and HTTP correctness fixtures

The following are release gates for this adapter. Tests can use deterministic fake child engines with independently controlled `alive`, `starting`, `unloaded`, `max_context`, slot counts, `last`, `progress`, `log_path`, and `gpu_pci`; no real GPU is needed.

1. **Config and PCI isolation.** Test count-based and named groups, one/zero replica disabled path, overlap/duplicate PCI rejection, missing/unavailable device and invalid group sizes. Build each child config and assert exact `gpu_pci`/`split_pci`, removal of parent-level replica config, no stale env override, independent log/profile paths, and unchanged original config. Verify regular layer-split config still produces one engine with its existing PCI list.
2. **Cache-aware routing and shared prefix.** Test identical token sequence hashes share only matching 64-token prefix; divergent suffix stops the match; cache cap stays bounded; loaded cached conversation wins when its saved-prefix advantage exceeds `LOAD_TOKENS * inflight`; cold ties distribute; dead children are excluded; long cached prefix can still lose to enough load. Ensure a routed conversation's follow-up can be answered by a different replica after load pressure without changing correctness because the whole prompt is sent.
3. **Cancellation and accounting.** With a non-batched fake child, hold its per-child lock, start a second request routed there, cancel that waiter, and assert bounded return, `inflight` restored, no leaked run lock, Service `queued`/`running` reaches zero, and no false prefix is retained for work never submitted. For an active streaming request, disconnect/cancel after first token and verify child cancellation, iterator `finally`, global request counters, per-replica running count, and slot view all settle. Repeat with two parallel replicas and one child that has batch slots; do not treat internal run-lock waiters as completed/running tokens.
4. **READY and startup rollback.** Fake child A reaches READY while child B fails READY/timeout; eager startup must close/kill every already-created process, start no listener, and report the failing replica index/device. For lazy mode, first load/request has a deterministic outcome and no orphan process. Test serial-start mode and concurrent-start mode without deadlock. A single READY child must not be advertised as a complete two-replica fleet unless partial startup is an explicit configured mode.
5. **Partial runtime failure and heal.** Once serving, kill one child: route new work to live children, keep service alive and return normal API responses, schedule at most one background heal per dead child, respect cooldown, and reset only that child's route-cache bits on successful restart. If one restart fails while another child lives, keep the live child and publish the failure with replica ID; if all are down, return the existing 503/server-error shape with a useful child owner. Restart the failed child and verify its next prompt is cold while other replica caches remain warm.
6. **Nonfinite ownership.** Make one fake yield a token then raise the current `EngineNonFinite`; ensure original API error handling is preserved, that child alone is forgotten because native nonfinite drops its own cache, all `inflight`/slot counts drain, and another replica's cached prefixes stay. Include a non-finite exception before any token too.
7. **Fleet context, slots, status and metrics.** Give fake children different READY contexts, one dead/one alive, then verify advertised max context is the minimum usable context; ensure requests above that limit receive the existing 400 instead of being routed to a smaller-context child. Verify global slot IDs are unique and map back to a replica in both `/metrics` and `/slots`; fleet `parallel` equals sum(child slots); running, waiting, `replicas_alive`, routed, prompt/read progress and `last` are attributable. Query metrics from a separate HTTP thread while requests run on both children to catch thread-local fallback to replica zero. Assert per-child logs/cursors are all visible and errors identify the responsible replica.
8. **SAVE/RESTORE and VRAM contract.** With `slot_save_path` enabled, `/slots/0?action=save|restore` and `/v1/vram` must fail as explicitly unsupported while a replica facade is active and call none of the children's `session_file`/`vram` methods. Confirm ordinary single-engine save/restore and elastic-VRAM APIs still work. If future product requirements need replica snapshots, require a new stable replica ownership selector and distinct per-replica files, then test RESTORE and next-turn routing back to the restored replica; do not infer owner from thread-local `current` or whichever process happens to be first.
9. **Settings and lifecycle APIs.** POST shared `/settings`, then submit requests routed to each child and assert they receive the same settings/sampling defaults. `/v1/load` loads all required children or reports the failed ones; `/v1/unload` unloads all children, is 409 while busy/queued, clears only corresponding caches, and is safe on repeated calls. `close()` must attempt to close every process even if one close raises; `unload()` should have an explicit best-effort/error policy instead of stopping at the first child. Test `before_load`, idle-unload and min-free checks with per-PCI fake telemetry so they are not executed only for group zero.

Existing upstream fake-engine tests cover the basics—group validation and route choice (`serve/test_replicas.py:18–145`), two-engine HTTP serving, conversations, slot summary and one dead-replica case (`:147–241`)—but do not cover several items above: queued cancellation/run-lock accounting, startup rollback, restart healing, per-replica error/log ownership, SAVE/RESTORE/V RAM refusal, PCI mapping, metrics thread ownership, `/slots` replica identity, and unequal contexts. Use those as additional required fixtures rather than assuming the existing test module establishes the full API contract.

## Limits and source pins

No actual multiple-SYCL-device launch or performance claim is qualified: this host has one GPU, and this report uses fake-engine/source evidence only. This is a contract and test plan, not an implementation review. Current immutable baseline hashes: `serve/server.py` `61267cad8dd7a9591fa99ad7ac3005f408ea08e9ed7fc81656872b45cbaac35f`, `setup.py` `c537e11811da54bea26e8feda28c9252054e13465ce4e68f16ffcfdffe22f462`, `serve/telemetry.py` `91d02627d67ca4208c77c7ccde6838b4a100f4cc52df4e4e74c196ac24b344d4`. Official audited source is pristine v0.1.43 at the parent-supplied pin; `serve/replicas.py` source details are cited by line above.
